newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ELLIOTT JUST MISSES DOUBLE CENTURY FOR AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ELLIOTT JUST MISSES DOUBLE CENTURY FOR AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Opening batsman Matthew Elliott fell one run short of a double- century as Australia established a huge first innings lead over England in the fourth test at Headingley on Sunday.
By lunch on the fourth day, the tourists were 501 for nine in their first innings, a lead of 329.
England knew they would face the prospect of having to bat through almost five sessions to avoid going 2-1 behind with two tests to come, at Trent Bridge and The Oval.

Elliott involuntarily joined the small band of players who have been dismissed for 199 in test cricket, when he was bowled by a yorker from Darren Gough. The tall left-hander had batted for 351 balls, striking 19 fours and three sixes.
England's players applauded him from the field, all too well aware that he had been dropped three times, including a sitter to Graham Thorpe at slip after making only 29.
Gough also bowled Jason Gillespie, his fifth wicket of the innings on his home ground, but there was little cheer otherwise for the Yorkshire crowd.
Australia, 373 for five overnight, took their scoring rate above four an over despite losing two wickets to Mark Ealham early on in the morning session.
He bowled wicket-keeper Ian Healy for 31 and had Shane Warne caught at slip for a duck in the same over.
Even with seven wickets down, England could not capitalise. Amid some shoddy fielding, tail-ender Paul Reiffel was allowed to rattle up 50 off 61 balls and was unbeaten on 54 at lunch.
Even Glenn McGrath, with a test match average of little more than three, was close to matching his previous highest score, on 20 not out.
One of the biggest disappointments for England was the bowling of debutant Mike Smith, who rarely troubled the batsmen and was without a wicket.
